source_name: Glassdoor / Indeed HU – employer-review and listing pages for payments firms
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: review volume, rating trajectory and self-reported office/role data act as a proxy for headcount churn and morale at Barion, Revolut HU and Wise Budapest; Indeed HU carries HU-language listings for the same employers.

source_name: Daily News Hungary – English-language coverage of Revolut HU expansion
why_relevant: English-language HU outlet reporting Revolut's local-branch build-out and hiring, including the MNB's push for a subsidiary and Revolut's decision against it — an entity-structure signal that directly shapes what and whom it hires in Hungary.

Hungarian fintech trade outlet with a dedicated GIRO Zrt. tag stream; carries CEO interviews (e.g. 'Exkluzív interjú a vezérigazgatóval') and event speaker listings that reveal who currently holds which role at the domestic clearing house.

Scheme-level Hungarian coverage; search results surfaced a Mastercard appointment for the Hungary+Slovenia market lead role via this outlet, indicating it publishes scheme country-manager moves that international newsrooms do not.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. official site - impresszum / company pages
why_relevant: The clearing-house operator's own site; impresszum and corporate pages name the sitting vezérigazgató and management, and press/news sections would carry organisational announcements first-hand.
Dedicated ATS/career portal of GIRO: open roles reveal headcount build-out, new function creation (e.g. instant-payment, qvik, security) and reorganisation before any press announcement.

Commercial mirror of register data with free entity pages for exactly the cell's actors (Global Payments Europe Hungarian branch, Mastercard Magyarország Kft.), including representatives and registered-data change history - easier to crawl than the statutory register.

Commercial credit/company-intel provider with per-entity pages for GIRO Zrt., Mastercard Magyarország Kft. and Global Payments' Hungarian branch; sells change-monitoring (cégfigyelés) products that can push officer-change alerts.

Additional free-tier company-data mirrors covering the same actors; useful as redundancy when one aggregator blocks or lags, and their 'kapcsolt személyek' views help map executives across multiple payment entities.

Employer page for the domestic clearing operator: posts announce appointments and new units, and the people/jobs tabs indicate headcount and function growth. Same pattern applies to Mastercard/Visa/Worldline/Nexi/Euronet HU pages.
Local-market site of a major acquirer/processor active in Hungary; product, merchant-services and press sections signal market entry, platform consolidation and local organisational build-up.

source_name: Worldline global media relations / press releases
why_relevant: Group-level newsroom where executive appointments (including regional/merchant-services leadership covering CEE) are announced first; complements the thin local newsroom.

source_name: Global Payments Europe Hungary (globalpay.hu) + GPN executive team page
why_relevant: Hungarian-facing site of the Global Payments Europe branch (a major processor/acquirer in HU) plus the group's executive-team page, which together cover local presence and group-level leadership churn driving reorganisation.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide Investor Relations - press releases & SEC filings
why_relevant: Euronet's European operations are headquartered in Budapest; IR releases, earnings calls and 8-K filings are the authoritative channel for executive changes, segment restructuring and ATM-estate decisions affecting the Hungarian deployer business.

Local operator site of the largest independent ATM deployer in Hungary (~600 ATMs per Hungarian media); about/news/career sections signal estate changes, fee-model shifts and local organisational moves.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség - member directory (GIRO member page)
why_relevant: The Hungarian Banking Association's member records list member institutions with named representatives; GIRO Zrt. appears as a member. The directory is a pointer to the institutional actor set and to the individuals who represent rails operators in industry bodies.

source_name: Mastercard Magyarország official site & Facebook page
why_relevant: Scheme's Hungarian presence; the 'Rólunk' section and the local social channel carry market-level announcements and occasionally introduce the local country/market lead - the only first-party HU-language channel for the scheme.

source_name: Hungarian general/business media covering payment-infrastructure operators (Origo, Kisalföld, Pénzcentrum, Magyar Nemzet)
why_relevant: Mainstream HU outlets cover ATM deployers and payment operators from a consumer angle (fees, estate size) and also report executive appointments at state-linked financial bodies; they provide corroboration and occasionally the only public trace of an operational change.

Dedicated 'Karrier' column plus a 'karrierhír' tag — exactly the A5 signal type. Privátbankár routinely publishes bank CEO departures/arrivals, often with rumour-stage reporting ('Megtudtuk, ki lehet az MKB Bank új vezére') that precedes official confirmation.

source_name: Világgazdaság (vg.hu) — Pénz és tőkepiac / magyar gazdaság
why_relevant: Long-standing business daily with strong access to state-owned financial institutions (MNB, EXIM, MFB, Diákhitel Központ). Covers political-appointment dynamics behind state-bank leadership, which corporate-origin sources never state.

Independent weekly/online; strongest of the cell on the negative side of A5 — layoffs, restructuring after mergers, forced exits, and political context of state financial appointments. Complements outlets that only run positive appointment news.

Best hu-language coverage of fintech/neobank leadership (Revolut Hungary branch head, Wise, challenger banks) and of people-centric rankings. Broke the Revolut Hungary branch-manager appointment as an exclusive ('közölte a Forbes.hu-val').

Pro-government-leaning economic portal that reliably republishes and expands bank appointment announcements, including for state-linked institutions; useful as a redundancy/confirmation channel and occasionally carries MNB-adjacent framing.

High-reach general news site whose Gazdaság section carries bank senior-management changes, including framing of the business rationale (e.g. AI/automation remit of a new MBH deputy CEO). Good for catching moves that specialist outlets treat as routine.

Investigative-leaning independent outlet; the strongest hu-language source for unannounced restructuring and layoffs inside financial institutions (broke Magyar Bankholding/MBH layoff plans and the MNB-linked redundancy round), i.e. A5 signals that never appear in press releases.

A dedicated, structurally uniform 'Appointments' feed in English covering Hungarian banks and financial firms (MBH, Citi Hungary, Bankholding). Ideal machine-readable spine for A5 because each item is a single appointment with name, title, institution and effective date.

Management-focused business portal with deep, long-running archive of bank deputy-CEO and division-head appointments (Raiffeisen, CIB, UniCredit, MBH). Strong for building historical career-path data on Hungarian bank executives, not just current-quarter news.

High-throughput business aggregator that republishes bank personnel press releases near-verbatim, including smaller institutions. Useful as a low-cost recall net and for catching items the flagship outlets skip.
